Random Parameters Count Regression Models

Source: R/countregrp.R
countreg.rp.Rd

Random Parameters Count Regression Models

Usage

countreg.rp(
  formula,
  rpar_formula,
  data,
  family = "NB2",
  rpardists = NULL,
  dis_param_formula_1 = NULL,
  dis_param_formula_2 = NULL,
  het_mean_formula = NULL,
  het_var_formula = NULL,
  ndraws = 500,
  scrambled = FALSE,
  correlated = FALSE,
  group_var = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  method = "BHHH",
  max.iters = 1000,
  start.vals = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  stderr = "normal",
  bootstraps = NULL,
  engine = "quadrature",
  keep_data = TRUE,
  panel_id = NULL,
  mix_draws = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

an R formula. This formula should specify the outcome and the independent variables that have fixed parameters.

rpar_formula

a symbolic description of the model related specifically to the random parameters. This should not include an outcome variable. If the intercept is random, include it in this formula. If the intercept is fixed, include it in formula but not in rpar_formula.

data

a dataframe that has all of the variables in the formula and rpar_formula.

family

the name of the distribution/model type to estimate. Default is "NB2". Options include "Poisson", "NB1", "NB2", "NBP", "PIG", "Sichel", etc. (see count_families for the full list). DW, DPO, HYPERPOIS and GAMMACOUNT solve their mean equation for every observation and draw, so they are much slower here than closed-form families; consider fewer ndraws while exploring. With "GP2", the dispersion must be nonnegative: the underdispersed GP2 requires \(1 + a\mu > 0\), which random parameters with unbounded support violate for some draws of every observation. Use "GP1", whose parameter space does not depend on \(\mu\), for underdispersed random-parameter models.

rpardists

an optional named vector whose names are the random parameters and values the distribution. The distribution options include normal ("n"), lognormal ("ln"), triangular ("t"), uniform ("u"), and gamma ("g"). Values are matched to the random parameters by name; every random parameter must be named. A single unnamed value applies to all random parameters. If not provided, normal is used. See Details for how each distribution's St.Dev parameter is defined.

dis_param_formula_1

a symbolic description of the model for the first parameter of the count distribution (e.g., ln(alpha) for NB2).

dis_param_formula_2

a symbolic description of the model for the second parameter of the count distribution (if applicable).

het_mean_formula

an optional one-sided formula for heterogeneity in the means of the random parameters. Each random parameter gets its own coefficient for each variable (named HetMean:<parameter>:<variable>), and the effect is additive: \(\beta_{ik} = \mu_k + z_i'\delta_k\) (Wood and Gayah, 2025, Eq. 2). For lognormal parameters the shift is on the log scale, and for gamma parameters it is multiplicative, \(\mu_k \exp(z_i'\delta_k)\), so the mean stays positive. The intercept is dropped.

het_var_formula

an optional one-sided formula for heterogeneity in the scales of the random parameters: \(\sigma_{ik} = \sigma_k \exp(s_i'\phi)\), with \(\phi\) shared by all random parameters. The intercept is dropped.

ndraws

the number of Halton draws to use for estimating the random parameters.

scrambled

if the Halton draws should be scrambled. Scrambled draws are generated from a random seed that is stored in the fit, so predictions reuse the same draws (and set.seed() before fitting makes the fit reproducible).

correlated

if the random parameters should be correlated. If TRUE, only normal distributions are used.

group_var

an optional variable name (string), or a vector with one value per row, defining the panel structure (repeated measures). If provided, each panel shares one draw of the random parameters, and the likelihood and standard errors account for the panel structure.

weights

the name of a variable, or a numeric vector, of frequency weights. With panel_id, weights apply to whole panels (the panel log-likelihood is weighted), so they should be constant within a panel.

offset

the name of a variable, or vector of variable names, to be used as an offset (summed when several are given). An offset can instead be given with offset() in formula; use only one of the two.

method

optimization method (e.g., "BHHH", "BFGS", "NM").

max.iters

maximum number of iterations.

start.vals

optional vector of starting values, one per parameter. Named values are matched to the parameters by name.

verbose

logical.

stderr

the type of standard errors: "normal" (Hessian-based, the default), "robust" (sandwich; clustered by panel when group_var is given), or "boot" (bootstrap that resamples whole panels and refits the model).

bootstraps

the number of bootstrap samples when stderr = "boot" (default 200).

engine

the numerical method for the mixed Poisson families PLN, PGE, PW and PLL: "quadrature" (default; adaptive quadrature on the log scale, accurate for every count), "halton" (the average over Halton draws used by flexCountReg 0.1.2 and earlier, kept to reproduce earlier fits; it is badly biased for counts far in the tail) or, for PLN only, "poilog" (the poilog package).

keep_data

logical; if FALSE, the training data are not stored in the fitted object. predict() then needs newdata.

panel_id

deprecated; use group_var.

mix_draws

with engine = "halton", the number of Halton draws for integrating over the mixing distribution of the PLN, PGE, PLL and PW families (inside each random-parameter draw). The default is min(ndraws, 200). Not used by the default engine = "quadrature", which integrates adaptively.

Value

An object of class flexCountReg which is a list with the following components:

  • model: the fitted model object.

  • data: the data frame used to fit the model.

  • call: the matched call.

  • formula: the formula used to fit the model.

Details

countreg_rp() is the same function as countreg.rp(), under a name that tools do not mistake for an S3 method.

Random parameter distributions. Each random parameter is \(\beta = \mu + \sigma \upsilon\), where the :Mean and :St.Dev estimates are \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\):

  • normal ("n"): \(\upsilon \sim N(0, 1)\), so \(\sigma\) is the standard deviation.

  • uniform ("u") and triangular ("t"): \(\upsilon\) is uniform or symmetric triangular on \([-1, 1]\), so \(\beta\) lies in \([\mu - \sigma, \mu + \sigma]\). Here \(\sigma\) is a half-width; the standard deviation is \(\sigma/\sqrt{3}\) (uniform) or \(\sigma/\sqrt{6}\) (triangular). Models fitted with version 0.1.1 or earlier used \([\mu - \sigma/2, \mu + \sigma/2]\) for the uniform; their \(\sigma\) is converted automatically in predict().

  • lognormal ("ln"): \(\beta = \exp(\mu + \sigma \upsilon)\), always positive. The expected value of \(\exp(x\beta)\) is infinite for \(x > 0\), so marginal (Exact or Simulated) predictions do not exist for observations with a positive value of a lognormal random parameter's variable. Use the variable's negative (so \(x \le 0\)), a gamma random parameter, or method = "Individual" predictions instead.

  • gamma ("g"): mean \(\mu > 0\) and standard deviation \(\sigma\), so the coefficient is always positive.

The mixing distribution of the PLN, PGE, PLL and PW families uses its own Halton dimension, independent of the random parameters' draws.

References

Wood, J.S., Gayah, V. (2025). Out-of-sample prediction and interpretation for random parameter generalized linear models. Accident Analysis and Prevention, 220, 108147.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Load data
data("washington_roads")
washington_roads$AADT10kplus <- ifelse(washington_roads$AADT > 10000, 1, 0)

# 1. Basic Random Parameters Negative Binomial (NB2)
rp_nb2 <- countreg.rp(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength,
                      rpar_formula = ~ -1 + speed50,
                      data = washington_roads,
                      family = "NB2",
                      rpardists = c(speed50 = "n"),
                      ndraws = 100,
                      method = "BHHH")
summary(rp_nb2)
#> Call:
#> countreg.rp(formula = Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + lnlength, rpar_formula = ~-1 + 
#>     speed50, data = washington_roads, family = "NB2", rpardists = c(speed50 = "n"), 
#>     ndraws = 100, method = "BHHH")
#> 
#> Model: countreg_rp | family: NB2 | optimizer: BHHH
#> Iterations: 29 
#> Convergence: successive function values within relative tolerance limit (reltol) 
#> 
#> Coefficients (standard errors: Hessian-based):
#>                Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)     -8.7552     0.4133  -21.18  < 2e-16 ***
#> lnaadt           1.0799     0.0500   21.58  < 2e-16 ***
#> lnlength         0.7564     0.0693   10.92  < 2e-16 ***
#> speed50:Mean    -0.7445     0.1687   -4.41  1.0e-05 ***
#> speed50:St.Dev   0.7170     0.2705    2.65    0.008 ** 
#> ln(alpha)       -1.3182     0.3052   -4.32  1.6e-05 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> 
#> Log-likelihood: -1082.98 | AIC: 2177.961 | BIC: 2209.844 
#> N: 1501

# 2. Random Parameters with Panel Structure (if 'site_id' exists)
# rp_panel <- countreg.rp(Total_crashes ~ -1 + lnaadt,
#                        rpar_formula = ~ speed50,
#                        data = washington_roads,
#                        group_var = "site_id",
#                        family = "NB2",
#                        ndraws = 100)

# 3. Generalized Random Parameters Model with Heterogeneity
rp_gen <- countreg.rp(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt,
                      rpar_formula = ~ -1 + speed50,
                      dis_param_formula_1 = ~ lnlength, 
                      het_mean_formula = ~ AADT10kplus,
                      data = washington_roads,
                      family = "NB2",
                      rpardists = c(speed50 = "n"),
                      ndraws = 100)
summary(rp_gen)
#> Call:
#> countreg.rp(formula = Total_crashes ~ lnaadt, rpar_formula = ~-1 + 
#>     speed50, data = washington_roads, family = "NB2", rpardists = c(speed50 = "n"), 
#>     dis_param_formula_1 = ~lnlength, het_mean_formula = ~AADT10kplus, 
#>     ndraws = 100)
#>

#> (Intercept)                  -8.4758     0.4390  -19.31   <2e-16 ***
#> lnaadt                        0.9559     0.0518   18.46   <2e-16 ***
#> speed50:Mean                 -0.7810     0.1872   -4.17    3e-05 ***
#> speed50:St.Dev                0.7417     0.2514    2.95   0.0032 ** 
#> HetMean:speed50:AADT10kplus   1.5599     1.2085    1.29   0.1968    
#> ln(alpha):(Intercept)        -1.1705     0.3638   -3.22   0.0013 ** 
#> ln(alpha):lnlength           -0.4738     0.2842   -1.67   0.0955 .

#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

#> N: 1501

# 4. Random Parameters Poisson Model with panel specification
rp_poisson <- countreg.rp(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt,
                      rpar_formula = ~ -1 + speed50,
                      het_mean_formula = ~ AADT10kplus,
                      data = washington_roads,
                      family = "POISSON",
                      rpardists = c(speed50 = "n"),
                      ndraws = 100,
                      group_var = "ID")
summary(rp_poisson)
